headline_marked: Bani Kapoor stuns in [[off-shoulder lehenga at India Couture Week]]
headline: Bani Kapoor stuns in off-shoulder lehenga at India Couture Week
summary: Bollywood actress Bani Kapoor closes Dolly J's 'Brahma' collection, inspired by the Himalayan Brahma Kamal flower, blending tradition with modern luxury.
details: Bollywood actress Bani Kapoor stole the spotlight at India Couture Week 2026, closing the show for designer Dolly J's 'Brahma' collection.
Bani Kapoor wore a stunning deep wine-colored lehenga featuring an off-shoulder blouse with a heart-shaped neckline, crystal embellishments, and a bold high-slit skirt.
The 'Brahma' collection is inspired by the rare Himalayan flower, the Brahma Kamal, symbolizing purity, spiritual awakening, and rebirth.
Designer Dolly J aimed to reflect the silent beauty and spiritual transformation of the flower through intricate craftsmanship, including Kashidakari needlework and tassels.
The collection's color palette ranged from deep red, antique gold, and earthy brown to midnight black and marine blue, representing the changing colors of the Himalayas from dawn to night.
Bani Kapoor complemented her look with minimal jewelry, including diamond drop earrings and a cocktail ring, paired with wavy open hair and dew-drop makeup.
The show highlighted the blend of traditional Indian craftsmanship with a contemporary vision for the modern woman's confidence and independence.
caption:
Bani Kapoor closes India Couture Week 2026 in a breathtaking wine-colored lehenga!

Bollywood actress Bani Kapoor stole the spotlight at India Couture Week 2026, closing the show for designer Dolly J's 'Brahma' collection.

Bani Kapoor wore a stunning deep wine-colored lehenga featuring an off-shoulder blouse with a heart-shaped neckline, crystal embellishments, and a bold high-slit skirt.

The 'Brahma' collection is inspired by the rare Himalayan flower, the Brahma Kamal, symbolizing purity, spiritual awakening, and rebirth.

Designer Dolly J aimed to reflect the silent beauty and spiritual transformation of the flower through intricate craftsmanship, including Kashidakari needlework and tassels.

The collection's color palette ranged from deep red, antique gold, and earthy brown to midnight black and marine blue, representing the changing colors of the Himalayas from dawn to night.

Bani Kapoor complemented her look with minimal jewelry, including diamond drop earrings and a cocktail ring, paired with wavy open hair and dew-drop makeup.

The show highlighted the blend of traditional Indian craftsmanship with a contemporary vision for the modern woman's confidence and independence.

headline_marked: 3 [[mortar shells recovered from ground]] in Lakshmipur
headline: 3 mortar shells recovered from ground in Lakshmipur
summary: The explosives were found by workers installing a pipeline near A S M Abdur Rob Government College.
details: Police recovered three mortar shells, described as rocket-like objects, from the ground in Ramgati Upazila of Lakshmipur on Wednesday.
The explosives were discovered by workers who were digging the soil to install a water pipeline near the eastern side of the security wall of A S M Abdur Rob Government College.
According to local reports, the workers initially re-buried the objects after finding them, but police were later notified and secured the area with red tape.

Ramgati Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Liton Dewan confirmed the recovery and stated that the objects are currently being kept safely at the police station under the direction of district police.
The Bomb Disposal Unit is expected to arrive at the scene to handle and dispose of the shells safely.
caption:
Three rocket-like mortar shells were found buried in the ground by pipeline workers in Lakshmipur.

Police recovered three mortar shells, described as rocket-like objects, from the ground in Ramgati Upazila of Lakshmipur on Wednesday.

According to local reports, the workers initially re-buried the objects after finding them, but police were later notified and secured the area with red tape.

Ramgati Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Liton Dewan confirmed the recovery and stated that the objects are currently being kept safely at the police station under the direction of district police.

The Bomb Disposal Unit is expected to arrive at the scene to handle and dispose of the shells safely.
